entryRoute.rationale: Unauthenticated root entry resolves to AuthScreen; authenticated and guest sessions resolve to HomePage.

items.name: Authentication Architecture
acceptanceCriteria: App resolves session state before selecting the application view.
Authenticated users enter AppShell.
Guest users enter AppShell with guest access state.
Unauthenticated users can access AuthScreen.
Login and ContinueAsGuest actions are defined.
Guest users may access routes with public or guest-allowed access levels only.

items.name: Root Application Architecture
acceptanceCriteria: App is the single application entry point.
App owns session resolution, route resolution, layout selection, and overlay hosting.
AppShell and StandalonePages are selected without duplicating the root layout.
Overlays are hosted at application level.

items.name: StandalonePages Architecture
acceptanceCriteria: StandalonePages uses a vertical Header, Content, and BottomAction slot layout.
Content is required and independently scrollable.
Header and BottomAction are optional per page.
BottomAction does not cover Content.
StandalonePages does not render AppShell BottomNav.

items.name: Bottom Navigation Architecture
acceptanceCriteria: BottomNav is rendered only in AppShell.
BottomNav contains Home, Explore, and Live Chat routes.
Active navigation follows the current route.
BottomNav respects the device safe area.

items.name: Routing Architecture
acceptanceCriteria: Every defined page has a unique route.
Dynamic route parameters are validated before page rendering.
Unknown routes render NotFoundPage.
Navigation preserves URL and active route state.
Protected routes use an explicit access policy.
Guest users can access public routes.

items.name: Design System and Responsive Layout
acceptanceCriteria: The application supports portrait mobile viewports from 320px and uses 390px as the reference width.
Header and bottom navigation remain outside the scrolling Content region.
Content scrolls independently.
Safe areas are respected by relevant fixed or edge-aligned controls.
No horizontal overflow occurs at supported viewport widths.
Design tokens are used consistently.

items.name: Overlay Architecture
acceptanceCriteria: Modal, BottomSheet, Drawer, and Toast are hosted centrally.
Overlays render above the active application layout.
Overlay visibility and state are centrally controlled.
Inactive overlays do not intercept interaction.
Dismissal behavior is defined for interactive overlays.

items.name: Production Technical Architecture
acceptanceCriteria: Components have explicit and maintainable responsibilities.
Component props use TypeScript types or interfaces.
Any usage is avoided or documented with a technical reason.
Loading, error, and empty states are handled.
Interactive components follow accessibility requirements.
Type checking completes without errors.
Production build completes successfully.
All defined routes are verified.

items.name: Component Registry and System Component Contracts
acceptanceCriteria: Every component reference in the blueprint exists in ComponentRegistry.registeredComponents.
AppLoadingState has an explicit responsibility and accessibility contract.
NotFoundPage has an explicit layout, recovery actions, and accessibility contract.
Component references are validated against the registry.

items.name: Single Active Page Rendering
acceptanceCriteria: AppShell.Content renders exactly one active page selected by the validated current route.
Non-active route pages are not rendered as active page content.
The active route remains the source of truth for page and BottomNav selection.

items.name: Deterministic Session and Layout Selection
acceptanceCriteria: Session resolution completes before access policy and layout selection.
Route classification and access policy determine whether AuthScreen, AppShell, or StandalonePages is selected.
Unauthenticated users default to AuthScreen when entering the application without an eligible public standalone route.
Valid public standalone routes can render without forcing AppShell or AuthScreen.
Unknown routes render NotFoundPage.

items.name: Route-Level Access Policy
acceptanceCriteria: Every registered route declares an access level.
Supported access levels are public, guest-allowed, and authenticated.
Guest users can access public and guest-allowed routes only.
Authenticated routes are accessible only to authenticated users.
Access is evaluated before layout selection and page rendering.
Denied protected routes follow the configured authentication redirect behavior.

items.name: Single Safe-Area Ownership
acceptanceCriteria: Application layout is the single owner of safe-area inset calculation and application.
Header, BottomNav, BottomAction, and edge-aligned overlays consume layout-provided insets.
Child components do not calculate or apply duplicate safe-area insets.
safeAreaAware=false means a child does not calculate insets independently; it still consumes insets supplied by the application layout.
Safe-area behavior is consistent across AppShell and StandalonePages.

items.name: Deterministic Entry Routing
acceptanceCriteria: The root entry route / resolves to HomePage in AppShell for authenticated users.
The root entry route / resolves to HomePage in AppShell for guest users.
The root entry route / resolves to AuthScreen for unauthenticated users.
Unauthenticated users may render registered public StandalonePages routes without being forced into AppShell.
Entry route behavior is explicitly defined and does not depend on implicit router defaults.

items.name: Unified Guest Access Policy
acceptanceCriteria: App guest access and Routing access policy use the same allowed access levels.
Guest users may access public and guest-allowed routes only.
Guest users are denied authenticated routes before layout selection or page rendering.
The canonical guest policy is public-and-guest-allowed-routes-only.
No conflicting guest access policy strings exist in the blueprint.

items.name: Explicit Route Access Declaration
acceptanceCriteria: Every registered route explicitly declares one supported access level.
Missing access declarations fail route registration or blueprint validation.
Invalid access values fail route registration or blueprint validation.
No implicit public access is granted to routes with missing access declarations.

items.name: Dynamic Route Parameter Contract
acceptanceCriteria: Every dynamic route declares its required parameter names and validation rules.
Required parameters are decoded and validated before the target page renders.
Empty, whitespace-only, missing, or malformed encoded parameter values are rejected.
Invalid dynamic parameters render NotFoundPage and never render the target page.
Dynamic parameter names match the corresponding route template.

items.name: Route-Driven Layout Resolution
acceptanceCriteria: Authenticated, guest, and unauthenticated session states do not independently force one layout for every route.
The matched route classification and evaluated access policy determine the eligible layout.
Registered AppShell routes render in AppShell when access is allowed.
Registered standalone routes render in StandalonePages when access is allowed.
Access denial occurs before layout selection and page rendering.
Exactly one active page is rendered after layout resolution.

items.name: Unified Guest Access Criteria
acceptanceCriteria: Guest users can access every registered public route.
Guest users can access every registered guest-allowed route.
Guest users cannot access authenticated routes.
App, Routing, F-01, F-12, and F-15 use one consistent guest access policy.
Access denial occurs before the target page or layout is rendered.

items.name: Safe Area Ownership Contract
acceptanceCriteria: Application layout is the sole owner of safe-area inset calculation and application.
Header, BottomNav, BottomAction, and edge-aligned overlays consume insets supplied by the application layout.
Child components do not independently calculate or duplicate safe-area insets.
The meaning of safeAreaAware is explicitly documented in the design system.
Safe-area behavior is consistent across AppShell and StandalonePages.
Safe-area handling prevents duplicate padding and content obstruction.

items.name: Blueprint Automated Validation
acceptanceCriteria: blueprint.json is valid JSON and conforms to the committed JSON Schema.
All component references exist in ComponentRegistry.registeredComponents.
All registered routes are unique and declare a supported access level.
Requirement IDs are unique and every requirement has at least one acceptance criterion.
Cross-section guest access and safe-area contracts are validated.
Mock user and product fixtures conform to their committed JSON Schemas.
Cross-reference and fixture validation runs through a repository validation script.
A GitHub Actions workflow runs validation on relevant pushes and pull requests.
Validation failures return a non-zero exit status and actionable error messages.

items.name: Mock Data Safety
acceptanceCriteria: mock/user.json contains a Guest fixture and an authenticated phone-and-password fixture.
User IDs are unique.
Guest fixtures have no credentials and use the guest auth provider.
Plaintext passwords are permitted only in explicitly marked mock fixtures.
Mock credentials are not production authentication credentials.
mock/products.json contains unique product IDs and consistent tour product structures.
Placeholder image assets are explicitly identified as mock-only placeholders.
Mock fixtures are not represented as production data or authoritative transaction records.

items.name: Repository Baseline Management
acceptanceCriteria: feature/blueprint-v1 is retained as the source baseline for Blueprint v1.2.0.
Blueprint v1.3.0 is developed on a dedicated feature branch.
Unchanged requirements are preserved and version changes are recorded.
Changes intended for main are reviewed through a pull request.
Non-mergeable pull requests are investigated before any merge decision.
Merge requires separate explicit approval.
Deployment requires separate explicit approval.

items.name: Repository Scope Definition
acceptanceCriteria: The repository scope is limited to application Blueprint documents, JSON Schemas, validation tooling, and mock data fixtures.
The Blueprint describes the mobile-only Travel & Tours application architecture.
Mock user and product fixtures remain under the mock directory.
Production React application source code is outside this repository implementation scope.
Backend, database, authentication-provider, payment-gateway, live-chat, and notification-service integrations are excluded.
New files must support Blueprint governance, mock data, or automated validation rather than introduce application runtime implementation.

items.name: Route Access & Booking Ownership
acceptanceCriteria: Booking history and booking detail are not publicly accessible without owner verification.
Authenticated users can read only bookings whose owner identity matches the authenticated user.
Guest users can read only their own bookings after backend verification of a guest booking proof.
Backend ownership verification is enforced on every request that reads booking data, not only on initial page navigation.
Cross-user and invalid guest-proof requests are denied before private booking data is disclosed.
Profile and notification routes require authenticated access.
Booking creation, checkout, and booking confirmation continue to support guest access.

items.name: JSON Schema Hardening
acceptanceCriteria: Finalized schema objects reject unknown properties where their contracts are explicitly defined.
User role and status values are restricted to documented enums.
Guest fixtures require role guest, guest auth provider, null phone, and null credentials.
Authenticated phone fixtures require role customer, phone auth provider, a valid international phone format, and a non-empty password fixture.
Product rating average is constrained to 0 through 5 and rating count is non-negative.
Product price, duration, availability, capacity, and remaining values have explicit types and valid bounds.
Schema validation accepts the existing valid mock fixtures and rejects invalid contract values.

items.name: Cross-File Validation
acceptanceCriteria: Requirement IDs are exactly F-01 through F-29 with no missing or duplicate IDs.
Every BottomNav item route resolves to a registered AppShell route.
Dynamic route parameter declarations exactly match parameters in their route templates.
Page IDs are unique across AppShell and StandalonePages page declarations.
User role, status, authProvider, isGuest, phone, and credentials are mutually consistent.
Product IDs and slugs are unique.
Product capacity and remaining values are non-negative and remaining never exceeds capacity.
Validator failures return a non-zero exit status and actionable diagnostics.

items.name: Mock Credential Safety
acceptanceCriteria: Mock credentials are explicitly classified as fixture-only and prohibited for production use.
Plaintext passwords remain limited to test fixtures and are never treated as production authentication credentials.
Repository documentation states that production authentication must use a backend identity provider, not mock/user.json.
Future production runtime code must not import mock fixtures as an authentication source.
Guest and authenticated fixtures remain available for local contract tests.

items.name: CI Reproducibility & Test Coverage
acceptanceCriteria: Validator dependencies are declared with exact versions and committed in package-lock.json.
GitHub Actions third-party actions are pinned to full commit SHAs.
CI installs dependencies using npm ci and runs schema and cross-file validation.
Positive tests verify valid baseline fixtures and contracts.
Negative tests verify malformed requirements, navigation routes, dynamic parameters, ownership policies, user fixtures, and product capacity constraints are rejected.
Workflow permissions are restricted to the minimum required read access.
CI results are associated with the exact commit SHA under test.
